_README: A WORKSHEET, not a record. Generated 2026-08-30 from the Betfair reference document,
which states plainly that it paraphrases rather than reproduces Betfair's text.
Every `verbatim` field is EMPTY on purpose. lib.rulebook.Clause refuses a clause with
no wording, so this file CANNOT be recorded until a person has opened each page and
pasted the actual words. That is the guard working: a paraphrase is a normalisation,
and normalising is exactly where two different rules become one and the arb becomes
`_where` says which page. `_look_for` says what the paraphrase claims is there, so you
know when you have found the right clause — it is a search hint and it is NOT the
record. Do not paste it into `verbatim`.
Then do the same for the SECOND book. Smarkets is the recommended pair.

clauses._where: Exchange Rules > Specific Sports Rules > Football/Soccer, plus the market's own Rules tab
clauses._look_for: Your reference: already-decided outcomes stand and all other selections void. If it is announced within 3 hours of kick-off that the game restarts within 3 days of the abandonment, bets stand. A temporary removal of players that resumes and finishes by midnight local time is NOT an abandonment.

Your reference: stands if confirmed to take place within the current or following 3 days of the original local kick-off DATE — but voids if the rescheduled start-time confirmation is not received within 3 HOURS of the original kick-off. Two different windows in one clause; quote both.

Your reference: stands unless switched to the OPPONENT'S ground, then voids. Major international tournaments deem all venues neutral. Note this differs from the General Rules team-sport clause — quote the football one.

clauses._where: General Rules > Periods of Time, and the market's Rules tab
clauses._look_for: Your reference: 90 minutes plus stoppage; extra time and penalties EXCLUDED unless stated. Stoppage-time events are deemed to occur at the end of regular time.

Your reference: the official result of the relevant governing body, ignoring later amendment EXCEPT one announced within 24 hours solely to correct a REPORTING error. New information within 48 hours may trigger resettlement; after 48 hours it is disregarded. Three separate numbers — quote the clause carrying all of them.

Your reference: Betfair may void all matched bets on a market for wrong competitor name, wrong number of outcomes, wrong exposure, or a cross-matching algorithm deployed. Note this is BROADER than a bookmaker's palpable-error clause, not narrower — it includes the venue's own matching error.

clauses._where: Betfair charges / commission pages — NOT the rules pages
clauses._look_for: Your reference explicitly does not capture this: commission %, market base rate and minimum stake live on the charges page and the API PriceLadderDescription. An exchange has no max-payout cap in the bookmaker sense, but commission on winnings is the equivalent truncation of the winning leg and must be quoted from the account.

clauses._where: General Rules > Managing markets in-play; Unmatched bets at the off
clauses._look_for: THE ONE YOUR DOCUMENT SURFACED. Your reference: unmatched bets are CANCELLED at the off unless set to Keep or Take-SP; there is an in-play bet delay; no part-suspension of individual selections in an in-play Exchange market; Betfair may cancel unmatched bets at any time. Quote the cancellation clause and the Keep/Take-SP options.

Your reference: reduced stake = stake x (expected winners / actual winners); the backer is paid reduced stake x traded price and the remainder goes to the layer. This is the worked case lib/arb.py already argues from — quote it exactly, it is what a bookmaker's very differently-worded clause has to be compared against.

Not applicable to soccer/h2h. Recorded here only so the topic is not left UNREAD by accident — if you are only doing football, say so in the verbatim field in your own words rather than leaving it blank.

Your reference: Cash Out is per-market not per-bet, is not guaranteed, and is reversed if the market later voids. An exchange does not restrict winning accounts the way a soft book does, which is the reason this pair was recommended — quote whatever the page actually says.
